head: c0f8460e4eb0d14a62b4ae60bd94b39c2258543f
summary:
All 14 acceptance criteria were met, checked against a fresh publish of the real exe. I did a clean single-file publish (139,768,472 bytes). The machine has no .NET 10 runtime, so the exe running at all proves it is self-contained. I ran it in the person's interactive session 1 at Medium integrity, against real filesystem trees. Build: 0 warnings. Core tests: 86 passed. The builder's WindowCases.ps1 passed all 12 cases.

Independent checks, using trees and datasets the builder did not write:
- My own tree had file and folder symlinks, a junction, a file with three hardlinked names, empty folders, and ü, ß and spaces in the root name. It gave identical OutcomeTitle and OutcomeDetail lines, and the same actualHeight of 369.22, in three runs: report mode, the new exe without --report (read in-process by a startup hook), and the exe from the commit before the slice (dc5d607). All three matched the tree.
- The repo's .dotnet folder: 5,578 files, 814 folders and 807,412,809 bytes, all exact.
- C:\Program Files: 78,509 files, 10,587 folders and 46 links matched my own count. The bytes first differed from a plain sum of file sizes by 3.1 GB. Counting each hardlinked file once by its file ID gave exactly 34,233,117,459, which is core.bytes, and the window showed that as 31.9 GB. The last timer tick read 65,963 files against 78,509 at the end, so the report holds the final ending and not a tick.
- Criteria 6 and 12 have no builder test. I drove them in the published exe through a startup hook:
  - Calling the Stop button's handler gave exit 0 and a 'Stopped:' report.
  - An exception thrown on the UI thread gave exit 70 in 474 ms, and the stale report and its .tmp were gone.
- Deleting the report's folder mid-scan gave exit 3 with no file and no .tmp. That is the final-write path O-017 says no test reaches.

O-001 and O-002, the two obligations owed to this stage, are discharged. The Fitness check passes: 10 rules.

Still open and owed to build-slice, not done in the tree:
- O-016: I reproduced it. Closing the window before the ending gives exit 0 and no report, which breaks WindowReport.cs's own 'Exit 0: the report was written'.
- O-017: the C-009 test still has no mid-scan run.
- O-018: the fitness.yaml header still says 'Five rules, eight entries' and has no xUnit twin.

None of these three breaks an acceptance criterion. The engine routes them.

checks.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 build FsAnalyser.slnx -c Release
checks.evidence: Build succeeded, 0 warnings, 0 errors. It was an incremental build (0.81 s).

checks.command: Remove-Item artifacts/publish -Recurse; eng/dotnet.ps1 publish src/FsAnalyser.App/FsAnalyser.App.csproj -c Release -o artifacts/publish; & 'C:\Program Files\dotnet\dotnet.exe' --list-runtimes
checks.evidence: Exit 0. The output is FsAnalyser.App.exe (139,768,472 bytes) plus 2 pdbs and nothing else. Machine-wide runtimes are 6, 8 and 9 only, and DOTNET_ROOT was empty, so the exe running proves it is self-contained.

checks.what: The session and token validate runs in (O-002)
checks.evidence: Session 1, Medium Mandatory Level, IsInRole=False, UserInteractive=True. The exe launched from here had SessionId 1 and a non-zero MainWindowHandle 381 ms after launch.

checks.what: The builder's window cases against the fresh publish
checks.evidence: PASSED: C-001, C-002, C-003, C-004, C-005, C-007, C-008, C-009, C-010, C-011, C-013 and C-014. Exit 0 in 42 s. C-002's scan took 1,608 ms, and CountersText after the last tick read 27,750 folders against 30,150 at the end.

checks.what: The Stopped ending (criterion 6), driven in the published exe
checks.command: DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS=<temp hook dll> FSA_HOOK_MODE=stop; eng/read-window.ps1 -Root <30,150-folder temp tree>
checks.evidence: The hook called MainWindow.OnCancel (the Stop button's Click handler) on the dispatcher 340 ms in. The result was EXIT 0, OutcomeTitle 'Stopped: <root>. This is only what was read before the stop, not the whole folder.', and OutcomeDetail '3 files and 750 folders; 0 links not followed' / '192.0 KB in files...', which equals core (status Cancelled, 3 files, 750 folders, 196,608 bytes). The hook also loaded into the reader's own pwsh process, where it did nothing.

checks.what: An unhandled UI-thread exception in report mode (criterion 12)
checks.command: FSA_HOOK_MODE=throw; Start-Process exe '"<big tree>" --report "<file with stale content>"' -PassThru; WaitForExit(60000)
checks.evidence: EXIT 70 after 474 ms with no hang and no dialog. The stale report was deleted and there was no .tmp. The command's tool exit was 1 only because the trailing Get-WinEvent query found no events.

checks.what: Report folder deleted mid-scan: the final-write path (criterion 9, the part O-017 says no test reaches)
checks.command: Start-Process exe '"<big tree>" --report "<temp>\out\r.json"'; wait for MainWindowHandle; Remove-Item <temp>\out
checks.evidence: The window handle appeared at 381 ms and I deleted the folder at 395 ms. EXIT 3 after 2,064 ms, with no file and no .tmp.

checks.what: Own tree: report mode vs the new exe without --report vs the exe from before the slice, all against the tree (O-001)
checks.command: compare.ps1: a tree with a file symlink, a folder symlink, a junction, a 3-name hardlink, empty folders and non-ASCII plus spaces in the root; eng/read-window.ps1, then a hook-read of the no-report window, new exe and dc5d607 exe
checks.evidence: All three read 'Finished: <root>', '6 files and 7 folders; 3 links not followed' and '640.0 KB in files, taking 640.0 KB on disk', with actualHeight 369.22. a==b, b==c and root==passed were all True. Both no-report windows were still alive 1.5 s after their ending, with a non-zero hwnd, and wrote no file. The guard refused my first version of the script (Remove-Item on a variable path); I rewrote it without Remove-Item.

checks.what: Real dataset I did not author: the repo's .dotnet SDK folder
checks.command: real.ps1 -Root <worktree>\.dotnet (Get-ChildItem enumeration vs eng/read-window.ps1 vs a hook-read without --report)
checks.evidence: Enumeration and window agree: 5,578 files, 814 folders, 0 links, 770.0 MB. core.bytes 807,412,809 equals the enumeration exactly. The no-report window text is identical.

checks.what: Real dataset: C:\Program Files (a space in the path, hardlinks, one unreadable folder, several ticks)
checks.command: real2.ps1 -Root 'C:\Program Files'; then file-ID de-dup of the LinkType=HardLink files through GetFileInformationByHandle
checks.evidence: The window read '78,509 files and 10,587 folders; 46 links not followed', equal to my own enumeration. The plain sum of file sizes (37,365,909,336) did not match at first. Removing the 3,132,791,877 duplicate-name bytes across 1,768 hardlinked files gave 34,233,117,459, which is exactly core.bytes, and the window showed that as 31.9 GB. CountersText at the last tick read 65,963 files against 78,509 at the end. The no-report window text was identical.
10 rules checked against 34 files; every declared rule holds, including the two from SL-023.

checks.what: MainWindow diff shows no rendering line moved (O-001)
checks.evidence: Additions only: the EndingShown event, the LastResult property, 'LastResult = null', 'LastResult = result' and two EndingShown?.Invoke calls placed after OutcomePanel.Visibility = Visible. No line was removed or changed.

checks.what: O-016: closing the window before the ending in report mode
checks.evidence: EXIT 0 after 486 ms, and no report file (the stale one was deleted). Exit 0 without a report contradicts WindowReport.cs's 'Exit 0: the report was written'. This is owed to build-slice, and App.xaml.cs has no Exit handler.

checks.what: O-017 and O-018 addressed in the tree
checks.command: Select-String of App.xaml.cs for 'Exit +=', of WindowCases.ps1 for 'MainWindowHandle', and of .taad/fitness.yaml for the header
checks.evidence: There is no Exit handler, and Test-C009 has no mid-scan run. fitness.yaml:11 still says 'Five rules, eight entries' and line 3 still calls it the twin of ArchitectureRulesTests.cs, while the SL-023 entries (line 143) have no xUnit twin. All three are owed to build-slice.

checks.what: Drive-root scan (C:\ or D:\) for the backslash criterion and the volume Coverage line
checks.evidence: Not run on purpose. It would read metadata across the person's own folders (D: holds 125 GB, and C: includes the OneDrive and profile folders), and the design says to test with a temp folder path plus a trailing backslash. That shape passed (C-013).

Not run, to avoid capturing the person's desktop. The evidence for rendering is IsVisible=true, ActualHeight 369.22 or 423.14 after Dispatcher.Yield(Loaded), and a non-zero MainWindowHandle in session 1.

checks.what: A real mouse click on Stop
checks.evidence: Driving another process's UI (UI Automation, SendKeys) is not allowed here. Instead, the Stop button's Click handler was called in-process through DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS.

criteria.criterion: 1. read the ending and totals from the published exe: a tree that finishes inside one timer interval (about 20 files, 4 folders)
criteria.how: C-001 passed on the fresh publish. My own 6-file, 7-folder tree and the .dotnet folder (a 45 ms scan) also matched an independent enumeration.

criteria.criterion: 2. read the ending and totals from the published exe: a tree large enough for many timer ticks
criteria.how: C-002: a 1,608 ms scan, last tick 27,750 folders against 30,150 at the end. C:\Program Files, a real dataset: 845 ms, last tick 65,963 files against 78,509 at the end, which matched my enumeration.

criteria.criterion: 3. read the links and hardlink lines: a junction and a hardlinked pair
criteria.how: C-003 passed. My own tree had a junction, a folder symlink, a file symlink and a 3-name hardlink, and read '3 links not followed' with the bytes counted once (640.0 KB). The 46 links in C:\Program Files and its hardlink-deduplicated bytes matched my own count to the byte, through core.

criteria.criterion: 4. read the not-Finished ending: the root does not exist
criteria.how: C-004: exit 0, 'Could not read <root>', core.status RootUnreadable, rootError 2.

criteria.criterion: 5. report when ShowProblem runs before any ScanResult (core null)
criteria.how: C-005 with a relative root: exit 0, 'Could not read', the reason given, and "core": null.

criteria.criterion: 6. read the Stopped ending: the scan is stopped by a person clicking Stop
criteria.how: The design marked this case not material and it has no builder test. I called MainWindow.OnCancel (the Click handler) in the published exe through a startup hook: exit 0, 'Stopped: <root>. This is only what was read before the stop...', and a detail equal to core (Cancelled). The click itself was simulated, not made by a person.

criteria.criterion: 7. launch with a fixture path containing a space, passed unquoted through Start-Process
criteria.how: C-007: the unquoted form gives exit 2 with no file and no .tmp; the reader's quoted form reads the full path. The real 'C:\Program Files' root also read correctly through the reader.
C-008 passed. Also, in my exit-70 and window-closed runs a pre-placed stale report was deleted and no .tmp was left.

criteria.criterion: 9. fail cleanly when the report cannot be written (parent missing, or the path is a directory)
criteria.how: C-009 passed for both startup shapes. I also deleted the report's folder mid-scan: exit 3, no file and no .tmp. That is the final-write path O-017 says no test covers.

criteria.criterion: 10. round-trip window text through the report file (non-ASCII, a no-break space, a dash)
criteria.how: C-010 passed: pure ASCII, \u escapes present, no byte-order mark, and Windows PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh agree. My ü and ß root also round-tripped exactly (root==passed True).

C-011 passed. On my tree, the new exe and the pre-slice exe without --report both stayed open with a window and wrote no file, and their window text was identical to the report's. Checked on the .dotnet and Program Files runs too.

criteria.criterion: 12. survive an unhandled UI-thread exception in report mode
criteria.how: The design marked this case not material and it has no builder test. I threw on the dispatcher through a startup hook in the published exe: exit 70 in 474 ms, no hang or dialog, stale report deleted, no .tmp.

criteria.criterion: 13. launch with a root that ends in a backslash
criteria.how: C-013 passed: a folder path with a trailing backslash through the reader, root equal to what was passed. A real drive root (C:\ or D:\) was not scanned; see not_reached.

criteria.criterion: 14. never wait on a person in report mode
criteria.how: C-014 passed: '--report' alone, '<root> --report' and '--report <file>' with no root each exit 2 inside 30 s, with no file.

obligations.evidence: The MainWindow diff is additions only, with no formatting or layout line moved. Architecture rule 2 holds (Fitness). On my own tree, the window text read in-process from the new exe without --report, from the pre-slice dc5d607 exe without --report, and from the report were identical (title, both total lines, actualHeight 369.22), and all matched the tree. On the .dotnet and C:\Program Files runs, the no-report text equalled the report. Launches without --report stayed open and wrote nothing.

The validate node's PowerShell runs in session 1 at Medium integrity, not admin. The exe it launched had SessionId 1 and a non-zero MainWindowHandle, and every report shows OutcomePanel.visible=true with actualHeight 369.22 or 423.14 after Dispatcher.Yield(Loaded). No screenshot was taken, so this is not pixel-level.
Owed to build-slice and not done: App.xaml.cs has no Exit handler. I reproduced it on the fresh publish: a hook-driven Close() before the ending gave EXIT 0 and no report file.
Owed to build-slice and not done: Test-C009 has no mid-scan run. I checked the behaviour by hand, and it is correct (exit 3, no file, no .tmp), but a regression would still go unnoticed.

Owed to build-slice and not done: .taad/fitness.yaml:3 and :11 still describe it as the twin of ArchitectureRulesTests.cs with 'Five rules, eight entries', while the SL-023 entries (line 143) have no xUnit twin.

not_reached: A real drive root (C:\ or D:\) in report mode. That run would reach the VolumeInUse/Coverage third OutcomeDetail line and the C:\ argv repair, and was not run so as not to read metadata across the person's own folders.
Pixel-level rendering. No screenshot was taken; the rendering evidence is WPF IsVisible, ActualHeight and a visible top-level window handle.
A real mouse click on Stop. The Click handler was called in-process through DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS instead.
An exception reaching the exit-70 handler after Shutdown(0) (the second half of O-016) was not exercised.
The on-disk size of the real datasets was not checked independently; only counts and bytes were.
Windows 10, other DPI scales, and non-interactive, RDP or locked sessions. Everything ran on Windows 11 26200, interactive session 1.
The contents of the unreadable-folders list. C:\Program Files had 1 unreadable folder, but schema 1 does not expose UnreadableExpander, so the report cannot show it.
Two WindowCases.ps1 runs at once while a source file has changed (the republish race the builder raised).
